sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Non-Constitutional & Non-Statutory**: Neither the Planning Commission nor the National Development Council (NDC) derived their authority from the Constitution or any Parliament-enacted statute; both were set up by executive resolutions of the Government of India.
• **Advisory Role of NDC**: The NDC was established specifically to secure cooperation of states in execution of plan policies, to strengthen and mobilize resources of the nation, and to ensure a balanced development across all regions.
• **Prime Minister as Ex-Officio Chairman**: Both bodies operated under the direct leadership of the Prime Minister, cementing central dominance in the initial decades of economic planning.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Five-Year Plans (FYPs) served as the central instruments formulated by the Planning Commission and ultimately approved by the NDC before implementation.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Created March 15, 1950; housed in Yojana Bhavan, New Delhi; led by PM as Chairman and a full-time Deputy Chairman.
Drafted Five-Year Plans, allocated central plan funds to states (Gadhgil Formula), monitored plan performance.
Tricky Prelims focus: Often confused as a statutory or constitutional body (like Finance Commission).
Created August 6, 1952; composed of PM (Chairman), all Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all states, and Administrators of UTs.
Supervised the working of the Planning Commission, considered national plans, and evaluated socio-economic policies.
Tricky Prelims focus: Not a part of NITI Aayog structure; its historical role as the 'super-cabinet' of economic planning.
Pre-independence milestone set up by Indian National Congress under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru.
Laid the intellectual groundwork for state-directed industrialization and economic planning in independent India.
Important historical linkage tested frequently in modern Indian history and economy overlapping sections.

items.definition: The formula approved by the NDC in 1969 (and later modified in 1990) for distributing Central assistance for State Plans among the various states.
A term often used by administrative experts (like K. Santhanam) to describe the overarching authority of the NDC over both central ministries and state governments in economic policy.
The historical New Delhi headquarters of the Planning Commission, symbolizing the era of command-and-control centralized planning.
The foundational executive directive defining NDC's mandate to review working of the Plan from time to time and recommend measures for achievement of aims and targets.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Centralized Delhi Hub**: Planning mechanisms were heavily concentrated in New Delhi, leading to a top-down 'one-size-fits-all' approach for diverse agro-climatic and regional zones.
• **Special Category States**: Hill states (North-Eastern states, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand) received special plan assistance configurations decided via NDC frameworks with higher grant-to-loan ratios.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Lack of flexibility for states, excessive centralization, resource misallocations, and declining relevance of NDC in the post-liberalization era of market-driven growth.
• **Policy Interventions**: Complete dissolution of the Planning Commission and NDC in 2014-2015, replaced by NITI Aayog to foster cooperative federalism through the Governing Council.

items.title: Mnemonic for Timeline of Major Planning Bodies
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'NPC Plans Development'
• **Decoded Meaning**: **NPC** (National Planning Committee 1938) -> **Plans** (Planning Commission 1950) -> **Development** (National Development Council 1952).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly sorts chronological sequence questions in Prelims without confusion.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember 'No Parliament Act, No Article'—both the Planning Commission and NDC were born out of Cabinet Resolutions, making them strictly non-statutory and non-constitutional.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the Planning Commission or the National Development Council are statutory bodies established under an Act of Parliament or constitutional bodies under Article 282/Article 263. Both statements are factually incorrect.

Mains Value Addition: In answers dealing with cooperative federalism or economic evolution, contrast the top-down coercive resource allocation of the Planning Commission/NDC era with the bottom-up competitive and cooperative federalism promoted by NITI Aayog's Governing Council.

keyTakeaways: The Planning Commission (1950) and NDC (1952) were executive/cabinet-created, non-constitutional, and non-statutory bodies that steered India's command economy.
The NDC served as the apex policy-making and review body for Five-Year Plans, incorporating all State Chief Ministers to bridge central planning with state execution.
Both institutions were dissolved in 2014, marking the transition from centralized planning to cooperative federalism via NITI Aayog.
